title: Measles Cases Hit New Record in U.S., as Vaccination Rates Wane - The New York Times
snippet:
Listen · 6:06 min

A patient with measles symptoms in South Carolina in January.Credit...Getty Images

Teddy Rosenbluth

By Teddy Rosenbluth

The United States has now recorded more cases of measles in 2026 than in any other year since the virus was declared eliminated in 2000, a grim sign that the country may be headed toward a new era in which the disease regularly sickens thousands every year. [...] On Friday, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention announced that there have been 2,318 confirmed cases of measles so far this year. The case count toppled the record set last year, when measles infected more than 2,200 Americans and killed two unvaccinated children. More measles cases have been reported in the United States in the last two years than in all the years from 2000 through 2024 combined. [...] Many of the cases reported this year were tied to a large outbreak in South Carolina that took root last October in a close-knit, evangelical Slavic community and quickly became the largest outbreak in the United States since 2000. The outbreak, which ultimately sickened nearly 1,000 people, was declared over by state health officials in April.

title: US sees highest number of measles cases in 35 years
snippet:
The US has recorded more measles cases over the past 18 months than the total number over 25 years before that.

The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to new infections. [...] # US measles cases reach 35-year high

Getty Images A fact sheet for measles sits on a table with a dark blue tablecloth, in a clipboard

The US has hit a 35-year high in measles cases, according to new figures from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

The US has seen 2,318 confirmed cases of measles in 2026, just seven months into the year, up from last year's high of 2,289, when two unvaccinated children died of the disease. [...] Last year, an outbreak among the Mennonite community in Texas killed two unvaccinated children, and an unvaccinated adult in neighbouring New Mexico.

Over the past month, Virginia and Pennsylvania have been dealing with new measles outbreaks, while the state of Utah is still responding to a cluster of infections that began last year.

Some 45 states have recorded cases.

title: 'Not trending in the right direction': US hits record high measles cases
snippet:
July 31, 2026

The US has confirmed 2,318 measles infections already this year, surpassing the entire tally of 2025 only seven months in and reaching the highest annual total in 35 years as vaccination rates decline. Reuters Erica Stapleton takes a look at Arizona, which is among states like Texas and Virginia reporting a high rate this year.

title: Map: Track measles outbreaks, cases and vaccination rates by state across the U.S.
snippet:
Measles, one of the most contagious viruses in the world, is regularly infecting people in the U.S. again.

Already in 2026 more than 2,300 cases have been counted, making 2026 the two year for measles infections in the U.S. since 2000.

NBC News is continuing to track confirmed measles cases across the United States, using Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data.

Measles case counts reached a 34-year high last year, and seven months into 2026, this year’s total is even higher. [...] Measles infection counts skyrocketed last year with 2,289 confirmed cases, which had been the most reported since 1991. This comes despite the virus being marked as being “eliminated” in the U.S. —a designation meaning it is no longer constantly circulating — in 2000. The U.S. is in danger of losing that status following a year of continuous spread of the disease.

Three people, including two young girls, died in the U.S. from measles last year. [...] The major outbreaks last year began with West Texas in February. In October, a measles outbreak occurred along the Utah and Arizona border. In all, the CDC recorded 48 measles outbreaks in 2025, up from 16 in 2024. So far in 2026, 35 measles outbreaks have been reported.

Childhood vaccination rates have been backsliding, leaving communities vulnerable to this deadly disease.

title: US measles cases hit 2,318 in 2026, surpassing last year's total: CDC - ABC News
snippet:
The majority of measles cases in 2026 have been confirmed among children and teenagers aged 19 and younger, according to the CDC. About one in 10 children under age 5 have been hospitalized.

About 93% of cases are among people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown, CDC data shows. [...] Previously, last year's total of 2,289 was the highest number of recorded measles cases in more than 30 years, CDC data shows. The new figure marks the highest number of cases recorded since 1991.

Cases have been confirmed in 43 states and the District of Columbia. Sixteen of this year's total have been among international visitors to the U.S., according to the CDC. [...] Meanwhile, 3% of cases are among those who have received just one dose of the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine and 4% of cases are among those who received the recommended two doses, according to the CDC.
